summary: Implemented update orchestration and the update command: lock-scoped diff, no-op, config-only recreate through the health-gated swap (never invoking the builder), and fetch/build/swap rebuild with build failures leaving the serving version untouched. Added 36 focused tests and extended swap's revert path to restore the previously applied config and environment. Typecheck, lint, focused suites, full 660-test suite, and build pass.

decisions: Desired config is an optional `desired`/`changes` input layered over config.toml; the in-memory desired spec is used for the operation and config.toml is written only after a keep.
A git-backed no-op fetches the configured ref and compares the checkout HEAD with the prepared commit; a moved commit becomes a rebuild so update-after-push is not silently ignored.
Config-only updates pass no state writer to the swap (which would set previous=current and destroy the rollback target); update writes health/container facts itself and preserves the image pair.

swapApp gained optional recoverySpec/recoveryEnvironment so a revert restarts the previous image with the previously applied port, bind, probe, volumes, and environment rather than the failed candidate settings.
A failed build or reverted candidate discards the disposable git checkout so a retry re-attempts the source instead of comparing the checkout with itself and reporting a false no-op.
A config.toml write failure after a successful keep is reported as a warning; the app is already serving the desired settings and the file can be re-applied by the next update.
When neither state.json nor a live container records an image, update builds and performs a bounded first start, mirroring add's failure cleanup.

warnings: src/cli/program.ts still registers update with the not-implemented placeholder; command registration is owned by cli-engineer and was not an expected output, matching the current state of add/logs registration.
The no-op source check requires a reachable configured ref for git apps; an unreachable remote makes update fail with the git/build exit code rather than reporting a no-op.
validationLimitations: The gated real-host update integration suite (tests/integration/update.test.ts, UPD-1.4) is owned by qa-engineer and was not run here; no real Podman, git, Railpack, or BuildKit was exercised by the unit suite.
payload.taskDescription: Implement update.ts and the update command. Load the app, acquire the lock, compute the diff, and execute the matching path: no-op, config-only recreate, or fetch plus rebuild plus swap. Apply config changes to the working config only after the operation succeeds, except for the candidate image reference which is recorded on success by the swap. Report what changed, what was skipped, and the final health. Exit 0 on success or no-op, 3 on build failure, 4 on a failed candidate, and 6 when the lock is held. Tests cover each diff class, build failure before any stop, lock contention, and reporting.
